newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fraser sees Sept qtr inflation within target.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fraser sees Sept qtr inflation within target.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Thursday that he expected September quarter inflation data to be released on October would be well within the RBA's target range.

"When the figure for the year to the September quarter is released next month ... we expect it to be well within the 2-3 percent band, and to remain there over the year ahead," Fraser said in a speech in Tokyo, a copy of which was released here.

"It was this encouraging inflation outlook, together with the less promising outlook for unemployment, which prompted the Reserve Bank to reduce official overnight interest rates by half a percentage point (to 7 percent) at the end of July," he said.

Fraser said inflation in Australia has averaged two percent in the past five years, compared with an average of eight percent in the 1980s. "Higher levels of productivity growth are helping the economy to grow more quickly than in the past without setting off inflation alarms," he said.

He said the prospect of sustained lower inflation had been strengthened by certain institutional changes, most notably the RBA's commitment to keep inflation under control - "a commitment which has been endorsed by current and past governments."

The RBA has said it is aiming to hold underlying inflation to two to three percent a year on average over the course of the economic cycle. "We see several advantages in formulating our inflation target in these terms," Fraser said.
"To begin with, it represents about as low a rate of inflation as any country is likely to be able to achieve over a sustained period of reasonable economic growth," he said.
"It is worth repeating that Australia has met this inflation target over the past five years while achieving relatively strong economic growth," Fraser said.
"This is in contrast to the experience in several other countries where low inflation in this period has coincided with very slack economic conditions," he said.
"Moreover, our formulation helps to achieve a reasonable balance between the Reserve Bank's twin objectives of low inflation and sustained growth," Fraser said.

"It does this because it recognises that inflation has a cyclical component and will tend to rise as growth strengthens, and to fall as growth slackens; in our view, any attempt to eliminate these cyclical movements in inflation would involve unwarranted losses in production and employment," he said.

"Finally, our formulation also avoids conveying the impression - as a narrow, hard edged target might - that inflation can be contained within bounds which, realistically, central banks cannot achieve if they are also to support growth in activity and employment," the RBA governor said.
Australia's underlying inflation rate in the year to June was 3.1 percent. Underlying inflation strips out volatile and season impacts on the consumer price index.
CPI inflation for the year to June was also 3.1 percent.
